lead.headline: Trump signs orders narrowing birthright citizenship
lead.dek: Two immigration actions follow the Supreme Court's 6-3 rejection of his first attempt in June.
body: President Donald Trump signed two executive orders Thursday narrowing who qualifies for birthright citizenship and restricting visas for visitors who come to the United States to give birth.

The citizenship order is narrower than the one the Supreme Court struck down. It excludes children born to people the administration designates as alien enemies, members of foreign terrorist organizations and agents of foreign governments, along with children whose parents obtained status by fraud, NBC News reported.

The court rejected Trump's earlier order 6-3 in June, upholding a broad reading of the 14th Amendment. Trump said he believed the new actions would be constitutional; the American Civil Liberties Union said it expects them to fail in court.

briefs.headline: Senate panel holds Fauci in contempt of Congress
briefs.summary: The Homeland Security Committee voted along party lines Thursday, a week after Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment at a July 29 hearing. The referral goes to the U.S. attorney in Washington.

briefs.headline: HHS proposes stripping most Head Start regulations
briefs.summary: The plan shifts authority to states, adds diet and fitness rules and caps overhead. The program serves about 700,000 children; comment runs 60 days.

briefs.headline: Student kills at least 5 at school near Bangkok
briefs.summary: Police said the teenager shot his grandparents at home, then opened fire at a school outside Bangkok on Friday, wounding 23. An earlier toll of six was revised to five.

briefs.headline: Uganda's parliament approves troops for Gaza force
briefs.summary: Lawmakers cleared a deployment to the 20,000-strong international force proposed by Trump's Board of Peace. Morocco, Indonesia and Kazakhstan have also committed troops.

briefs.headline: Cholera and drone strikes grip besieged Sudanese city
briefs.summary: El-Obeid, a city of about 500,000 in North Kordofan, is sheltering more than 100,000 displaced people. At least 59,000 have died since Sudan's war began in 2023.

briefs.headline: Disaster jobless aid opens for Lewis and Upshur counties
briefs.summary: Workers who lost jobs in the July 21-22 storms, tornadoes and flooding may file through Oct. 2, with benefits payable through Feb. 6.

briefs.headline: Charter board weighs rules for closed rural schools
briefs.summary: A new law lets communities convert closing schools into in-person charters and creates micro schools tied to colleges. A bylaws vote slid to Sept. 10.

regional.item: Officials broke ground Thursday on a $40M, 124-bed nursing center in Barboursville expected to bring 150 jobs.
Seventeen cars of a CSX grain train derailed in South Charleston Thursday morning, with no injuries reported.

fishing.line: 116 cfs and steady, 1.72 ft - prime wading water.
Sound highs 3:22 a.m. and 4:06 p.m.; water 80.6F at Wrightsville Beach, 25 miles down the coast.

briefs.headline: Mudryk plays for Chelsea after 20-month doping ban
briefs.summary: The Ukraine winger came on in the 82nd minute of Wednesday's 1-0 friendly loss to Juventus in Hong Kong, his first outing since testing positive for meldonium.

briefs.headline: Colts extend Jonathan Taylor for 2 years, $44M
briefs.summary: The running back's deal carries $39M guaranteed and a $22M average, just under the figure Bijan Robinson signed with Atlanta this week.

briefs.headline: X-ray telescope finds sign of a 1936 quantum prediction
briefs.summary: Light from magnetar 1E 1547-5408 was polarized far more than expected, evidence of vacuum birefringence. NASA called it a signal further observations must confirm.

briefs.headline: Trial finds acetaminophen and ibuprofen equally safe in infancy
briefs.summary: A randomized trial of nearly 4,000 New Zealand babies found neither drug raised eczema or bronchiolitis at age 1. Researchers will follow the children to age 6.
